Definition: from G1537 and a form of G1061 (compare G1548); to marry off a daughter:--give in marriage.
BiblicalUsage: This is the same compound verb as the last word, to give a daughter in marriage, and it stands in the Textus Receptus at both of the flood passages. In Matthew the days before the flood are spent marrying and giving in marriage, and in Luke the people of Noah's day ate, drank, married wives, and were given in marriage until the day Noah entered the ark. The Greek text used for this study carries only the plain verb to marry in both verses, so this compound is a reading of the older printed text.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ordinary life is no shelter from judgement, because the flood came on a day like any other, when people were marrying and giving in marriage.
RelatedTopics: Judgment; Marriage; Fear of the Lord
